backend_bugs_for_main_agent.issue: Admin-side quote PDF endpoint not implemented. PDF generation infra (reportlab) already exists in portal.py and profit_analytics.py — port the pattern to a new /api/quotes/{id}/pdf route.
Admin-side invoice PDF endpoint not implemented (only /api/portal/invoices/{id}/download exists for portal customers). Add admin equivalent so staff can download invoice PDF without portal login.
Production-floor work-ticket PDF not implemented. Spec'd in checklist 6.4.
No central listing endpoint for AI tools and their credit costs. Frontend likely hardcodes the list. Consider exposing for dynamic UI + admin pricing visibility.
PDF/image invoice field-extraction endpoint not implemented. Was in spec but no route exists.
No server-side clear-chat endpoint. Currently chat history is client-managed (passed back via conversation_history field). Document this as 'by design' or implement a sessions store.
Generated PDF is only ~2KB — minimal layout. Spec calls for >5KB richer content (line items, branding, tax breakdown, totals, watermark). Confirm intent vs upgrade content.
Payroll PDF is referenced in the spec but the param-based PDF response is not implemented. Confirm if needed for prelaunch.

code_review_critical_comments: portal.py /appointments/request: email-send is correctly wrapped in try/except so SendGrid failure does NOT block appointment creation — good. Graceful degradation when email_service.is_configured()==False also confirmed (no crash).
ai.py is 3,183 lines — consider splitting into ai_assistant.py, ai_image.py, ai_email.py, ai_voice.py for maintainability (file-size code-review rule >700 lines).

ai.py /assistant relies on client to pass conversation_history; there is no server-side session persistence. This is fine for stateless usage but means clear-chat is impossible to enforce server-side and a malicious client can replay arbitrary history. Document or harden.
credit checks in ai.py do preview→success-deduct correctly (no double-charge on failure). log_failed_ai_usage path covered.
Several AI routes do `from emergentintegrations.llm.chat import LlmChat` inside the function — fine for lazy load but inconsistent with module-top imports elsewhere.
portal invoice PDF is generated inline (portal.py uses reportlab directly). Repeated reportlab boilerplate in profit_analytics.py and portal.py — DRY-violate. Extract to services/pdf_renderer.py.
No unicode/CJK font registered with reportlab — non-ASCII customer names may render as boxes in actual PDFs. Use TTFont registration (DejaVuSans or Noto) to be safe.
seed_data_creation: Created during run: 1 appointment (auto-rejected), 1 unicode customer (José Niño with 北京 line item, deleted after test). All cleaned up. Email_logs rows from appointment-request flow are real prod-data and intentionally retained as evidence.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 135 closes Tier 6 backend-only sweep. Test file: /app/backend/tests/test_iteration135_tier6.py (20 tests, ~22s, hits each AI endpoint at most ONCE, image-gen NOT invoked to save credits — only route presence verified). Key findings: (a) appointment-request email path is solid — email_logs collection has 2 sent/202 rows, no crash on unconfigured SendGrid; (b) AI assistant multi-turn context works via client-supplied conversation_history (no server-side session store); (c) several PDF endpoints from spec are NOT_IMPLEMENTED — quote PDF, invoice PDF (admin), work-ticket PDF, payroll PDF; (d) /ai/tools list, /ai/extract-invoice, clear-chat are also NOT_IMPLEMENTED. Portal invoice PDF only ~2KB (minimal). For Tier 7+ testing, see Section 17 user-only list above and the backend_bugs_for_main_agent for prelaunch gaps.
